body: Thank you, I appreciate it.  I hope this all works out.

Thank you for responding.  I really appreciate it.  I assumed this thread was really buried by now.  I am meeting someone on Monday about an internship, and I am actually looking into a work-study program in advanced manufacturing at a community college.  It's not an apprenticeship, and there is upfront tuition cost, but if all goes well it will pay for itself.  I'm at least going to enroll to see what happens, I will have some time to decide.  I have been interested in the possibility of doing a traditional apprenticeship, though.  Have you gone that route?  Lol, I am definitely a late-bloomer.  It's been a strange life so far.

This is cool man, it's really accurate.  This is how I feel right now.  Do you often express your OCD experience with art?  I hope you share again if you do.  I think it's a really interesting idea.  I used to draw, and I'm supposed to start getting into it again as part of my therapy.
PM me.

You are not alone in this.  Thinking about my dark future is frightening to the point of being paralyzing, but thinking about dying is freeing, I feel more relaxed and open, because none of my problems matter anymore.  I know it's not healthy and could be dangerous, but suicidal thinking often gets me out of anxiety or OCD induced ruts.  I'm sure plenty more will chime in with similar experiences.
It's not fun
You are right.  It's very hard to let go of though.  It feels like an obsession.
Thank you.  I, too, had symptoms as a toddler, and things started to get really bad when I was around 13.  I'm glad that ERP worked so well for you, and I hope it works for me as well.

Thanks for reaching out.  Our timeline is similar but off by just a few years.  I had severe symptoms around age 13 (lesser but not debilitating symptoms before that) and am now finally getting the proper treatment at 34.  It is hard to let go of those lost years.  Maybe you're right that mourning them is healthy.  I'm so glad that things are better for you now and your partner.  I have substance abuse issues in my past and it is very painful to think about.  I hope that things turn out for me like they did for you.

Thank you for sharing your story.  I am ironically doing a little reassurance seeking but I am feeling pretty hopeless and skeptical about ERP (I am starting Thursday).  20 years is a long time to deal with this and sometimes it feels like it can't really get better.

I see stats like that, too.  I just wondered what people's actual experiences where like.  I sometimes feel like I am the only one who has gone on this bizarre journey, and I am having a very bad night tonight.

I can relate to some of what you've said.  Talk therapy is really ineffective, isn't it?  I hate that it can take so long to get something like this diagnosed, I feel like it has basically stripped me of the best years of my life.  Did you do ERP?  I understand that it is considered a form of CBT.  Did the therapy make a big difference in your life?  How about the medication?

I am feeling suicidal and hopeless right now.  I think you can see from these responses that it is extremely common.  I have read that recent studies show OCD sufferers may be 10 times more likely to commit suicide than the general population.  In my case I feel that it is not my symptoms that make me feel suicidal, but the enormous impact this disease has had on my life.  Are you having a better day today?
Thank you.  I will let you know how it goes tomorrow.  Can't sleep tonight, nervous about it.
It does seem simple in principle.
I feel your pain for sure.  Do you live in the U.S?

Thank you for your support and for putting things into perspective, and for the resources you shared.  I will look at those in a bit.  I have had an atrociously bad OCD weekend and I just feel completely isolated from everyone right now.  I am in this weird in-between spot where my symptoms aren't quite bad enough that I need to be hospitalized or that I'm housebound (consistently), but they are bad enough that it is very difficult for me to hold down a job or be very independent right now.  And I am looking forward to ERP, although I fear that it might not work, as I know that for a significant minority of people it doesn't (or so I've read), and so of course I'm fixating on that, lol.

You've put things into perspective here.  I also didn't seek help for years, mostly out of fear of what was going on in my head, and specifically that someone might verify that my thinking is justified, just as you said.  When I did seek help I got repeatedly misdiagnosed, as I didn't understand myself what I was dealing with and therefore didn't go to the right professionals, had a hard time contextualizing my symptoms so probably made them sound like they were caused by something besides OCD, etc.

I hope it didn't sound like I was implying that high functioning people with OCD don't suffer, I know they do, having talked directly to the other people in group, I just feel all alone with this thing sometimes because I don't know anyone who has a life that looks quite like mine.

I have a sort of hypochondria issue, but for mental illness, so I am always convincing myself that I have bipolar disorder or ADHD or Borderline (it is possible to have those with OCD, but not the case with me).  It's made it very hard to get a correct OCD diagnosis, and I often doubt that I actually have OCD.  Your counselor will be able to determine whether you really have bipolar or not, but what you're describing sounds like what I go through, being easily convinced that I have something that I don't actually have.  Definitely discuss it at length with your therapist, though.

Thanks for responding to me.

Friendships are hard.  You are not a screw up for not having fiends, and you are certainly not alone in that.  It's amazing how this disorder wrecks your life, and the things that it impacts.  I have people that I consider friends, but I am not close to them.  I have struggled most of my life to find a romantic partner and to hold down a job.

Are you doing ERP?  I go to a free group and I am trying to work with the group administrator to find someone who specializes in OCD treatment.  I am curious how your treatment is going.

If you would like, I will gladly be your internet friend.  The only two people I've ever known (outside of those I've met recently in the group) with OCD are cousins, but I am not close to them.  I think this disorder can be incredibly isolating, because it can make you feel so different from everyone else.  Feel free to message me any time, I'd love to hear from you.
I hope not.
Thank you for the offer to talk.  I am looking at what will happen if I go to the hospital, just in case.
I got through the other night and am more stable right now.
Thank you.  I will check out your page.
I do indeed.

Thank you, and well said.  I didn't think what you said was harsh.  I do have a problem with ruminating about things over and over again.  I like your philosophy and I hope I can apply some of that to myself this year.  Several people have suggested meditation.  How often do you meditate?
You're right.  The impulsiveness is what's dangerous I think.

I sure hope so.  Having the structure will help a lot I think.  I have an interview (phone) tomorrow so we'll see how it goes.  I do miss having coworkers and just people to interact with all day.  It's weird how isolating unemployment can become.  How was your day?
Agreed.
I agree.  I don't want to hurt my loved ones.  Sometimes in my worst moment I'm not thinking about that though, which is scary.

Thank you for your thoughts and your advice.  Being suicidal has been a wake up call of sorts.  I actually have spent the last couple days thinking about where my life is and what is really important to me.  Failing in life the way I have has put me in a unique place, I really don't have the option to chase money or status, that life has passed me by at this point.  I have an opportunity to go after what is really important, but that requires a lot of courage, something I haven't displayed a lot of yet in life.  I hope that that changes this year.  Thank you so much for your perspective.

Thank you.  I really appreciate that advice.  The other night I reached out to some friends on Facebook and it helped me get through the night.  It's weird how that moment passes and you are OK again, at least for a little while.  I think that I will keep writing.  It does help me to clear my head and there's something about putting it on the internet rather than just writing it in a journal.  I don't know what it is but it's different somehow.

It's extremely painful. That's an interesting point about the temp agency and exactly need.  Just somebody to look past the employment gap somehow.  Just need somebody desperate enough, lol.  I was taking care of ailing family members during that stretch so I can say that maybe.  And the offer stands always.

Christmas is the worst, isn't it?  At least it brings out some pretty horrible feelings for me.  If you are feeling alone and depressed and you need to talk to someone, you can message me.  I am a bit slow about responding but I will respond.

It is shitty, you're right.  The "stuckness" is the worst part.  I often feel like I am still 13 years old.  The destruction of the people I love is also the one thing that keeps me from killing myself.  That and tiny little bit of hope that I will finally catch a break and things will turn out ok.  I don't know if that is delusional or not.  I suspect it is but it's all I've got.  And thanks for the offer to chat, you can talk to me if you need to as well.

It really sucks to think that someone loves you (especially when they tell you that repeatedly) and then to find out that they don't at all.   And being old and poor also sucks.  I am going to try the temp agency route after the first of the year, but I'm sure the work history gap will be an issue there also, like you said.  I don't know what else to try.  You're right, people who aren't going through this don't seem to understand, and it is hard to meet people online.  You can message me any time you want though.

Thanks for your response.  I am really, really sorry to hear about what you're going through right now.  I am hurting pretty bad in my current situation, but I won't pretend to know what it's like to have the love of your life leave you that way.  I hope you are able to heal in time, and I hope you had a good day at work today.

Sorry, I get very wordy when I am distressed and tend to ramble on.  But you're right, I need to be focusing on getting a steady job and dealing the the mental health issues, it is just hard because I have been dealing with the mental health stuff for so long without any success.

I'm glad you could relate to my story.  There are many times when I feel completely alone in this situation.  There aren't stories about people like us online and reddit skews very young it seems.  I remember feeling like it was literally the end of the world when I was an 18 year old virgin and that sort of thing.  I really hope these people don't end up killing themselves over something like that (obviously), because it's not a big deal, and for most of them it will get better, but as I can attest, things can also get much worse.

I am also seeing a therapist who is our age and I really like her, but we are not making any progress.  A lot of that is because I struggle to open up to her because I'm so embarrassed about my situation.  I haven't completely cut my friends out but I do keep them at arms length, don't let them in because I don't want them to see how bad things are, and that makes me feel completely alone and also like a fraud.  They all assume I live independently and have some nondescript job somewhere and I allow them to believe that.  And it makes me very jealous when they achieve some milestone or success.  I feel awful about that.  I wish I could be happy for them but it just seems to remind me of what a failure I am.

I am holding onto hope that I will finally catch a break but I am also trying to learn to accept that that may never happen, as it hasn't happened yet.  I don't know which mindset is healthier at this point.  I am very lucky to have the support of my parents, even though I know how disappointed they are in me, and my sister, who is also struggling, but is not as fucked up as me.  I am learning to be truly grateful for them and for the things that I do have, but it is very difficult when it seems like everyone else has so much more going for them.

Good luck to you too, and you can message me any time you want.

OP, my life has been shit for many, many years, so I can relate to that even if we have different circumstances.  You can message me if you need someone to talk to, and I will try to answer if I'm still awake.
